contents: # Roster (uhifadhi/roster-module) — who is due on watch, where and when: the
# rotation a post or a team runs, the duties it generates, the swaps and
# absences that change them, and the on-duty presence read back from the area.
# NOTHING BELOW IS REQUIRED. Every key has a default, and the tree is CLOSED, so
# an invented key fails at compile time rather than being ignored. Delete the
# whole `roster:` key and a fresh installation still runs — it simply uses the
# vocabulary written out below.
# WHAT THIS MODULE STANDS ON. Everything that is not about rosters arrives with
# `uhifadhi/uhifadhi`: the per-area catalogue this module's tile is filed in
# (registry), the page frame and the configure page its sections hang off
# (shell), the people a duty names (team), and — load-bearing here — the AREA,
# which owns the station a watch is stood at, the posting that puts somebody
# there, the check-in and the presence derived from it. This module owns the
# plan and reads the presence; it computes none of it.
roster:
# Which catalogue category the Roster tile is filed under in every area.
# OPERATIONS, because a roster is the rangers' OWN work — `pressure` in the
# catalogue means human pressure ON the ecosystem.
module_category: operations
# THE SHIFT VOCABULARY A NEW AREA IS SEEDED WITH — and read exactly once
# per area, the first time anything asks for its list.
# IT IS A SEED AND NOT THE LIST. "One list for the whole area" is ruled:
# the running vocabulary is rows an area edits on the module's own Settings
# section, where a shift is renamed freely and CLOSED rather than deleted,
# because a past month has to keep the word that described it. Changing a
# line here therefore affects areas that have not been looked at yet, and
# leaves settled ones alone — which is what you want, and worth knowing
# before you edit it expecting otherwise.
# The KEY is stored on every duty and must never change once duties carry
# it; the label is only what a screen shows. A WINDOW MAY CROSS MIDNIGHT —
# `night` runs 18:00 to 06:00 — and a duty belongs to the calendar day its
# watch BEGINS on, so a night watch is one duty and two blocks on a day
# board. `off` is reserved: a rotation's ring spells a stood-down day that
# way, so a shift of that name would make every stored cycle ambiguous.
shifts:
- { key: day,    label: Day,         start: '06:00', end: '18:00' }
- { key: night,  label: Night,       start: '18:00', end: '06:00' }
- { key: office, label: Office,      start: '07:30', end: '16:30' }
- { key: radio,  label: 'Radio night', start: '18:00', end: '06:00' }
# THE VALUES A NEW AREA SETTING, STATION WATCH OR ROTATION STARTS AT — read
# when one is CREATED and never at display time. What a station or an area
# actually runs at afterwards is its own stored value, edited on a screen;
# a config value read at display time would silently override whatever a
# park set, and the override would be invisible.
defaults:
# Positions per hour, per handset. It trades against the catchment: a
# wide catchment tolerates a slow interval, a tight one does not — at
# 2 km and 60 min a ranger can leave and return unseen — and every
# minute taken off it costs battery in a place with no mains.
ping_interval_minutes: 30
# How long a post may go quiet before it reads as LATE. Per station in
# the product: a gate that never closes and a rim post reached once a
# fortnight cannot share one.
silence_window_minutes: 120
# How long before late becomes OFFLINE. Offline is a fact about the
# post and never about its people, and it clears itself when something
# lands — nothing is dismissed by hand.
offline_after_minutes: 1440
# How close a ping has to be for a claim of "at post" to read as
# verified. It never hides anything: a claim whose positions fall
# outside it is SHOWN AND FLAGGED as unverified, never corrected and
# never turned into an absence.
catchment_metres: 1500
# How far ahead a NEW rotation generates duties. The editor offers six
# weeks, three months and the end of the year; all three write a number
# of days, because a stored preset called "end of the year" would mean
# something different every January.
horizon_days: 42
when@dev:
roster:
dev_tools: true
when@test:
roster:
dev_tools: true
# THE CYCLE EDITOR'S CONTROLLER. This module ships one Stimulus controller,
# `roster--rotation`, and a recipe cannot merge into `assets/controllers.json`
# — Flex writes that file from the package's own `assets/package.json`, which
# declares the controller enabled. If the ring, the per-day counts or the pool
# do not respond on the Rotation section, that is the line to check:
#   bin/console debug:asset-map | grep roster-module
#   cat assets/controllers.json          # expects "@uhifadhi/roster-module"
# The page still READS without it: the rotation renders as it stands and only
# the editing is inert, so a failed asset compile is a page somebody can read
# rather than a row of dead buttons.
# AFTER INSTALLING, in this order:
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate   # the module's own tables
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:diff      # must say "No changes detected"
#   bin/console registry:sync                 # put Roster in the catalogue
#   bin/console cache:clear
#   bin/console asset-map:compile             # not optional
# THIS MODULE SHIPS ITS OWN MIGRATIONS, and that is the fleet ruling: the tables
# are the bundle's, so the SQL that creates them arrives with it and an
# installation writes no version for `roster_*`. `doctrine:migrations:diff`
# stays what you run for the entities YOU write, and after an update of this
# package it must report no changes — churn there is a bundle bug, not
# something to route around.
# THEN SWITCH IT ON. A module is installed but PARKED: the registry seeds it
# into every area's ledger switched off, and every page of it answers 404 in an
# area that has not taken it — 404 and not 403, because a parked module is not
# withheld, the area is simply not running it. Turn it on per area from the
# area's Modules page.
# AND GRANT IT. This module declares one concern, `roster`, and
# grants it to nobody: changing how an area runs its roster — the rotations,
# what each post's watch expects, the settings — needs it. Assign it in Team's
# permission matrix. Reading the pages needs nothing.
# A HEAVY CONSOLE RUN GOES WITH `--no-debug`. A warm-up that walks the registry
# collects every query of every request while the debug kernel is on, and on a
# small box that is how a `cache:warmup` meets the memory limit.
# WHO THE DUTIES POINT AT — and why there is nothing to write here.
# Several columns on this module's tables name a PERSON: who is on the watch,
# who is away, who recorded the absence, who edited the day. None of them names
# an account class; all of them are mapped to
# `Uhifadhi\Contracts\Entity\UserInterface`, and the core's TeamBundle — the
# package that actually provides the accounts — states the resolution from its
# own bundle. Whoever knows the answer states it, so an ordinary installation
# writes no doctrine line at all.
# YOU WRITE A LINE ONLY TO DISAGREE — to name your own account class instead. It
# goes under the `orm:` key ALREADY IN config/packages/doctrine.yaml, beside
# `mappings`, never as a second `doctrine:` key in that file:
#   doctrine:
#       orm:
#           resolve_target_entities:
#               Uhifadhi\Contracts\Entity\UserInterface: App\Entity\Person
# WHAT THIS MODULE DOES NOT DO, said once so nobody goes looking for it.
# There is NO on-duty field on any form here, for any role, including an
# administrator. Presence is derived from a ranger's own check-in and the pings
# that followed it — both the AREA's — and this module reads that derivation
# rather than keeping a second one. A roster says who is DUE at a post tonight;
# it never says who is there.
# Roster module screens (uhifadhi/roster-module) — the module's tabs and the
# three sections of its configure page, all nested under their area:
# /areas/{uuid}/modules/roster/…
# The addresses are the controllers' own, declared as attributes beside the code
# that answers them. This file is what mounts them, and it is yours: remove the
# import and the screens are gone from `debug:router` with nothing left behind.
# THE CONFIGURE PAGE ITSELF IS NOT HERE. `/areas/{uuid}/modules/roster/configure`
# belongs to the core's shell, which mounts it once for every surface in the
# platform; this module's three sections sit BESIDE it — /rotation, /watches,
# /settings — precisely so they cannot race the frame's own route.
roster:
resource: '@UhifadhiRosterBundle/src/Controller/'
type: attribute
